clue.text: Sad feeling, Brexit dealer beyond hellish place

indicators.note: the dealer's name comes after, i.e. beyond, the hellish place in the answer

parts.note: Dis is the classical underworld, and Dante's city of Hell
Theresa May, the UK prime minister who negotiated the Brexit deal

explanation.surface: Gloom at the Brexit deal on offer, which looks worse than hell.
explanation.definitionFit: Dismay is a sinking feeling of distress and discouragement, a kind of sad feeling.

clue.text: Almost entirely posh character ascendant in novel

indicators.note: in a down clue, ascendant means the pieces are read from the bottom upwards
almost means the word for entirely loses its final letter

parts.note: entirely means all, as in 'all wrong'
U is the old shorthand for upper-class, posh usage
a card is a character, an eccentric person

explanation.surface: A grand figure rising to the top of a novel almost completely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' trims ALL to AL; AL + U + CARD gives ALUCARD, which 'ascendant' turns upwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Bram Stoker's Gothic horror story of the Transylvanian count is a famous novel.

clue.text: See 11
As scenario briefly unfolding

indicators.note: unfolding means the remaining letters open out into a new order
briefly means the word scenario is cut short, losing its last letter

explanation.surface: Describes how a story plays out as a summary of events.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' drops the final O of SCENARIO; 'unfolding' rearranges SCENARI. 'As' looks like a little link word, but it is the chemical symbol and so the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: As is the chemical symbol for the poisonous element, so the symbol defines the element itself.

clue.text: Sex in urinals once ordered for a pound, say?

indicators.note: ordered means the letters are put into a new arrangement

parts.note: male is one sex

explanation.surface: A lewd scene of men in old public toilets, sorted out for a quid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sex' is replaced by its synonym before the shuffle. 'pound' is not money but a pen for stray dogs or seized livestock.
explanation.definitionFit: A pound is a pen where stray dogs or impounded livestock are kept, an example of a place confining beasts.

clue.text: Sister taking so long to dismiss a church representative

indicators.note: taking means the sister picks up the next piece after her

parts.note: a nun is a Sister in a religious order

indicators.note: to dismiss means the letter a is sent out of the goodbye word

parts.note: ciao is Italian for goodbye, so long

explanation.surface: A nun takes ages getting rid of a clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to dismiss' drops the A from CIAO, leaving CIO.
explanation.definitionFit: A papal nuncio is the Pope's ambassador, representing the Catholic Church abroad.

clue.text: Without rivals, unable to play?

definitions.meaning: read as 'lacking a match', with no game to take part in

explanation.surface: A champion so far ahead that nobody will compete with them.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unequalled means no-one can match you; split, the word means lacking a game, so you cannot play.

clue.text: Concert venue providing some basic singing, including opera, though not needing to

indicators.note: including means the singing holds the shortened opera inside it

parts.note: la-la is wordless, simple singing

indicators.note: though not needing means the letters of the word to are dropped from the opera's name

parts.note: Tosca is Puccini's opera
taken as written

explanation.surface: A recital hall offering simple vocals and opera, unnecessarily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'though not needing' removes TO from TOSCA, leaving SCA, which 'including' puts in the middle of LALA.
explanation.definitionFit: Milan's famous opera house is a world-renowned venue for concerts and opera.

clue.text: Tons and tons in 10 across, perhaps?

definitions.text: Tons and tons in 10 across, perhaps?

parts.words: Tons and tons in 10 across, perhaps?
parts.note: a ton is a hundred runs in cricket, and 10 across is a cricket match, so huge totals of runs in it

explanation.surface: Lots and lots of something in the second test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tons' suggests weight, but in cricket a ton is a century, a hundred runs; several in a Test match make a big total.
explanation.definitionFit: Centuries piled up in a Test match describe a large total of runs recorded on the board.

clue.text: See 15
Part of series back on screen

parts.note: to second is to back or support, as with a motion
to screen is to test, as in medical screening

explanation.surface: An episode of a show returns to TV.
explanation.walkthrough: A series here is a cricket series, where Test matches are played; 'on' just places the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket series is made up of several Test matches, and the next one after the first is one of its parts.

clue.text: Good houses giving poor boys food

parts.note: bum as an adjective means of poor quality
sons are boys
eats is slang for food

explanation.surface: Kind households feeding poor lads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor boys' looks like one idea, perhaps tramps, but it splits in two. 'houses' are theatre audiences, and a good house is a full one.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatre slang for paying audience members; a good house in a theatre is a well-filled auditorium.

clue.text: Dividing the country, is monarch Republican or Unionist?

indicators.note: dividing means these pieces split the country's name in two

parts.note: Iran is a country
HM stands for His or Her Majesty

explanation.surface: A question about whether a king would split a nation's politics.
explanation.walkthrough: In Northern Ireland politics, Republicans want a united Ireland and Unionists want to stay in the UK; a man from the island could be either.
explanation.definitionFit: A man from Ireland might be a republican or a unionist, so either is an example of one.

clue.text: Sweet thing ending in harmony, some land slipping back into water

indicators.note: into means these letters go inside the body of water

parts.note: a lake is a body of water

indicators.note: ending in means take the final letter of harmony
slipping back means the measure of land is read backwards

parts.note: an acre is an area of land

explanation.surface: A soothing piece ends in harmony while some ground slides back into the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversed land measure, ERCA, follows the Y, and the pair go between the second and third letters of the water.
explanation.definitionFit: A gateau built of sponge tiers with filling between them is a sweet treat.

clue.text: See 4
Not quite finished opening a wine vessel

indicators.note: not quite finished means the word for opening loses its final letter

parts.note: a vent is an opening
cava is Spanish sparkling wine

explanation.surface: Opening a bottle of wine before it is quite empty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not quite finished' cuts VENT to VEN. 'vessel' looks like the bottle, but it is a blood vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Either of the two great veins carrying blood back to the heart is a large blood vessel.

clue.text: Scottish town that may be lit

definitions.meaning: A town in Caithness in the far north of Scotland
a candle's string is set alight

explanation.surface: A Scottish place that might be illuminated.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a Caithness town in northern Scotland and also the string in a candle that you light.

clue.text: Reportedly handle like a car, perhaps?

indicators.note: reportedly means the word for handle is said out loud to give the answer

parts.note: to wield is to handle a tool or weapon

explanation.surface: Supposedly, the steering of a car.
explanation.definitionFit: A car runs on wheels, so it has them fitted, as does a cart or a bicycle.

clue.text: Bit of a bloomer around setback for experienced politicians

indicators.note: around means the flower part goes round the reversed piece

parts.note: a stamen is part of a flower, a bloomer
set back gives the word set reversed

explanation.surface: A gaffe around a political setback for veteran politicians.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' suggests a blunder, but here it is a flowering plant. 'setback' is SET read backwards, TES.
explanation.definitionFit: Seasoned, respected political leaders are called statesmen, unlike mere politicos.

clue.text: Has unruly lad gone climbing? Put one's foot down here

indicators.note: has means the tree holds the rearranged lad within it

parts.note: a lad gone climbing is up a tree

indicators.note: unruly means the letters of lad are disorderly, rearranged

explanation.surface: Asking whether a naughty boy has climbed up a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: The jumbled boy, ADL, ends up inside the thing climbed: a lad who has gone climbing is up in its branches.
explanation.definitionFit: A foot-operated lever on a sewing machine or spinning wheel is a place where you press with your foot.

clue.text: Near middle, back from Asia?

indicators.note: middle means take the central letters of near

parts.note: the stern is the back of a ship

explanation.surface: Somewhere near the centre, coming back from Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: Asia is in the East, so something from there can be called oriental or from the East.

clue.text: See 23
One's possessed coin made in error

indicators.note: in error means the letters of coin made are set wrongly, scrambled

explanation.surface: A coin struck by mistake is owned by someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's possessed' reads as ownership, but it means one who is possessed by a devil.
explanation.definitionFit: A person possessed by a devil or evil spirit is a demoniac, so 'one is possessed' describes him.

clue.text: Retired setter with head on stamp

indicators.note: retired means the word for the setter goes back, read in reverse

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as me
the boss is the head of an organisation

explanation.surface: A retired crossword setter, along with a chief, on a postage stamp.
explanation.walkthrough: Crossword setters often refer to themselves in clues as 'setter', giving ME; 'stamp' here is a verb, not postage.
explanation.definitionFit: To emboss is to stamp a raised design onto paper or metal.

clue.text: Film director: goat less domesticated

parts.note: a billy is a male goat
wilder means less tame

explanation.surface: A filmmaker considered a goat that is less tame.
explanation.definitionFit: The man who made Some Like It Hot was a Hollywood director.

clue.text: Doctor done with flu and visibly embarrassed, struggled

indicators.note: doctor as a verb means to tamper with, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: red in the face from embarrassment

explanation.surface: A GP who has had flu and blushes was out of his depth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a noun, a physician, but it is a verb, the anagram signal for DONE and FLU.
explanation.definitionFit: To flounder is to struggle clumsily, as in deep water or a difficult task.

clue.text: Song enjoyed, though disheartened

indicators.note: disheartened means the word for enjoyed loses its central letter, its heart

parts.note: liked means enjoyed

explanation.surface: A song that was enjoyed, though it made you feel low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' takes the middle K out of LIKED.
explanation.definitionFit: A lied is a German art song, typically for voice and piano, as by Schubert.

clue.text: Dull seeing bottom within limits of decency

indicators.note: within means the bottom goes inside the limits
limits of means take the outside letters of decency

parts.note: the rear is the bottom, the backside

explanation.surface: It is boring to see a backside within decent limits.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dull and gloomy, lacking any interest, is dreary.

clue.text: African understanding why many avoiding the borders

parts.note: ken is knowledge or understanding, as in 'beyond my ken'
Y is the letter whose name is said like why, a crossword convention

indicators.note: avoiding the borders means drop the first and last letters of many

explanation.surface: An African's grasp of why many people stay away from the frontiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'avoiding the borders' reduces MANY to AN.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from Kenya, an East African country, is an African.
